claim: The reference list is generated from structured entries and a pinned Crossref cache rather than typed, and the repository form and the venue form are rendered from the same entries.
status_note: A hand-written reference list is where a volume number typed once becomes a volume number nobody checks again. Two styles typed separately would be two chances to disagree about the same record.
value: 38 entries; 13 carry a DOI and take authors, title, journal, volume, pages and year from the Crossref cache; 7 take title, affected parts, status and edition from the pinned DICOM status table; the remaining 18 carry fields no registry holds. Both renderings come from the same entries.
floor: not applicable, this row reports a documentary artefact and not a validator rate
dropped: nothing; every entry renders in both styles and a check asserts neither rendering contains a double period, a stranded colon, residual markup or a collapsed page range
notes: Generating the list corrected four things a hand copy carried: a Crossref record that splits Imperfect Forward Secrecy from its subtitle, one that returns the dcmqi title wrapped in markup, one that returns a single-page abstract as 3493-3493, and Crossref's lowercasing of 10.1158/0008-5472.CAN-21-0950.

claim: The submission package is assembled from the manuscript documents by code, and every venue requirement that can be computed from the package is met.
status_note: Assembly is a transformation of what is already written. Nothing in the generator authors a sentence carrying a measurement, so a number wrong in the package is wrong in the manuscript and fails the build there.
value: 8 documents, 6 figures as EPS with PDF and PNG beside each, 1 supplementary table; 14 requirements checked automatically and all met; 4 named as not checkable here; 15 placeholders listed by file
floor: not applicable, this row reports a package against a checklist and not a validator rate
dropped: the package is Markdown and not Word. Producing .docx needs a package that is not in env/requirements.lock, and adding one to a pinned measurement environment to typeset a paper is not a trade this project makes. Typesetting, font size, page numbering and line numbering are not done and are named in the checklist

claim: The venue requirements the package is built against were read from the venue's own guidelines on a stated date, and two of them bind hard enough to change the paper.
status_note: A package built against remembered requirements is a package built against the requirements of some other journal.
value: Journal of Imaging Informatics in Medicine, guidelines read 2026-08-03. Double-blind review, so two manuscript files are required. Abstract 150 to 250 words. 4 to 6 keywords. No more than 3 displayed heading levels. References numbered in order of first citation, in the venue's own style. Figures named Fig1 onward, EPS preferred for vector graphics, fonts embedded. Declarations before the reference list. LLM use documented in the Methods.
dropped: the backup venue's requirements are not encoded; the checklist names which items would change
notes: The two that bind hardest are the ones that were not anticipated: the review model is double-blind, and the abstract limit is a third of what the repository abstract runs to.

claim: The abstract submitted is a 249 word form, and what the short form drops is listed rather than left to a reader to notice.
status_note: A shortened abstract is a sampling decision. The project rule that silent truncation reads as full coverage applies to prose as much as to a census.
value: 249 words against a 150 to 250 limit; the repository abstract is 695 words and is not the one submitted
floor: not applicable, this row counts words and not validator findings
dropped: five things, each listed in abstract_venue.md with where it survives in the paper: the concentration in the object-weighted rate and the leave-one-class-out figures, the name and counts of the excluded class, the reliability kappa and its intra-instrument disclosure, the declared grading sensitivity, and the ceiling, the mechanism and the drafted correction proposal

claim: The blinded copy carries no author name, affiliation, identifier or repository URL, and the paper is nonetheless identifiable from its content, which is stated rather than left implied.
status_note: What masking guarantees and what it cannot are different claims. The second is the one a checklist usually omits.
value: 25 declared tokens and phrases masked, 0 surviving; an independent case-insensitive search for the ten strings a reviewer would type returns nothing; competing interests and author contributions are replaced by a pointer to the title page rather than masked in place; the 5 self-citations are left blank so the numbering is identical in both copies
dropped: content-level anonymity is not attempted and is not achievable: the paper describes a public repository and reuses the method of two prior papers by the same author
notes: Masking the company name out of a competing-interests paragraph that still described the author's employment produced something that looked blinded and was not. The paragraph is replaced by a pointer to the title page, which the venue does not send to reviewers.

claim: The venue requires a link to the imaging data used, and the package supplies every collection in the measured classes with the source DOI the archive index records for it.
status_note: The requirement is written for The Cancer Imaging Archive. This study reads the Imaging Data Commons, whose index carries a source DOI per collection, so the requirement is met in the archive's own terms rather than argued around.
value: 126 collection and source-DOI rows over the eight measured classes and Segmentation Storage, covering 62 distinct source DOIs and 481,750 series
floor: not applicable, this row reports an index read and not a validator rate
dropped: nothing was downloaded and no count in the paper depends on this table; it exists so a reader can reach the data. A collection whose index rows carry no source DOI appears with an empty DOI rather than being omitted
